title: Choose Habit Shaper’s visual world
question: A calm, private journal is the pinned direction. Confirm it or choose a different visual world before implementation.

options.label: Private Daybook
options.lineage: quiet personal day planners and Apple-like native utility interfaces
options.thesis: A private place for one person to return to their day with clarity, not perform productivity.
options.viewport: A generous white sign-in panel sits in a quiet field; Habit Shaper and one short promise lead, with the form as the only action.
options.risk: Too much restraint could make early MVP states feel unfinished unless typography and spacing stay precise.
options.case: Best on audience identification and product clarity: it directly matches the requested calm, individual companion.

options.label: Personal Record
options.thesis: Each habit becomes a private record, indexed with disciplined calm.
options.viewport: A near-black account surface organizes identity as one small catalog entry with strict index lines.
options.risk: Fuses poorly because the coded, austere identity can make a private daily companion feel cold.
options.case: Strong distinction, but loses product clarity to the quieter daybook direction.

options.label: Visible Count
options.thesis: Streaks become physical counts that glow once a day is complete.
options.viewport: A compact sign-in panel is framed as an instrument with one softly glowing count display.
options.risk: Fuses poorly because visible instrumentation shifts attention toward streak mechanics before the product has earned it.
options.case: Memorable, but too playful and mechanically styled for the requested private journal.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar SaaS account page, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: A centered card with logo, title, fields, and one blue button.
canonCard.risk: Clear but forgettable; it does not express Habit Shaper’s private, reflective purpose.
